original_title: Small-Molecule Activation Reshapes the Catalytic Conformational Landscape during Ca2+ ATPase Turnover
title: Watching a small molecule rewire SERCA's catalytic cycle in real time
blurb: Time-resolved X-ray solution scattering, MD and kinetic modeling on SERCA, the sarco/endoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ ATPase, show how the activator yakuchinone A speeds up the pump's turnover by redistributing which transient conformations it visits during the cycle, not by locking in some new static structure. A real-time look at how an activator actually works, which is a rarer thing to see than the usual before/after crystal structures.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Thiol-ene Radical Polymerizations of Regio - and Stereo -Isomers of a CO2-Derived δ-Lactone Leading to High Molar Mass Polythioethers
title: Fixing CO2-derived lactone's one bad habit before building polymers from it
blurb: The straightforward product of CO2/butadiene telomerization, EVP, carries an alkylidene group that tanks thiol-ene reaction kinetics, so dithiols only ever gave low molar mass polythioethers. Photo-deconjugating EVP into its isomer DVP removes that snag, and the same thiol-ene chemistry then runs cleanly to high molar mass polythioethers carrying up to 20 wt% CO2. A regiochemistry fix rather than a new reaction, but it's the fix that was actually blocking the useful polymer.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Repurposing a biosynthetic enzyme for imaging UDP-glucose dynamics in living systems
title: An old bacterial enzyme repurposed into a UDP-glucose sensor
blurb: They gutted H. pylori's UDP-glucose pyrophosphorylase and used cpGFP insertion plus directed evolution to turn it into UGluS, a ratiometric sensor that responds specifically to UDP-glucose over its metabolite cousins. About an 18-fold excitation-ratio swing, a 32.5 µM dissociation constant, and it works in live cells, which is the part that usually kills these things.

original_title: Photoisomerization Triggered Temporal Control in Invertase Activity Through pH Modulation
title: A light switch that flips pH to run an enzyme on a timer
blurb: An azoheteroarene photoswitch shuttles pH up and down on command, and that shift is used to turn invertase activity on and off with light instead of chemical titration. The actual engineering problem was making the photoswitch bistable and thermally stable across a wide pH range in real aqueous buffer, which is where most of these molecules fall apart.

original_title: Biology meets chemistry for improved porphyrin synthesis
title: Fermentation plus biocatalysis for porphyrins
blurb: Stitches fermentation, biocatalysis, and conventional chemical derivatization into one porphyrin synthesis route, letting biology handle the steps that organic chemistry usually does clumsily.

original_title: Scalable Alkylation-Cyclization Strategy for Bridgehead-Functionalized Fused Tetrahydrofurans
title: A one-pot route to bridgehead-functionalized fused THFs, by the gram
blurb: Cyclic β-ketoesters plus 1,2-dibromoethane under K2CO3/18-crown-6, alkylation and cyclization in a single step, no nasty reagents, and it scales to multigram batches. Covers five-, six-, and seven-membered carbocycles plus some heterocycles, the kind of unglamorous versatility that actually gets used.

original_title: Boronium-Based Ionic Liquids: From an Unusual Main-Group Cation to Functional Ionic Materials
title: Boron gets its own ionic liquid cation
blurb: A look at boronium salts, tetra-coordinate boron cations paired with the right ligands and anions, built on the L1L2BH2+ scaffold that two decades of work have turned into genuine room-temperature ionic liquids. Low glass-transition main-group materials from a cation most people would've reached past for lithium or imidazolium.

original_title: CoMn Nanosheets Mediate Water-Driven Luminol Electrochemiluminescence via Coupled Electrocatalysis and Nanozyme Activity for Biosensing
title: Letting water do the oxidizing for luminol ECL
blurb: Cobalt-manganese nanosheets that drive oxygen evolution and act as an oxidase-mimicking nanozyme at the same time, converting water into superoxide and singlet oxygen in situ to light up luminol electrochemiluminescence. Sidesteps the usual reliance on dosed hydrogen peroxide and sluggish dissolved-O2 activation that's bottlenecked these biosensors.

original_title: Antiaromaticity for Through-Space Molecular Thermoelectricity
title: Antiaromatic molecules turn out better at moving heat-driven charge
blurb: Antiaromatic Ni(II) norcorrole stacks outperform their aromatic counterparts at thermally driven charge transport, because pushing the electronic stabilization out to the surface instead of locking it inside the ring lets neighboring molecules couple more strongly. That coupling is strong enough to support unusually thick stacks, the opposite of what the aromatic playbook would predict.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: SPLAT: An Event-Specific System Response Model for Continuous-Domain List-Mode TOF PET
title: A TOF PET model that stops binning photons into boxes
blurb: SPLAT builds the forward and adjoint operators for list-mode time-of-flight PET straight from each event's continuous position, timing, energy, and depth-of-interaction data, skipping detector-coordinate binning entirely. They work out an anisotropic Gaussian version of the response kernel, trading a coarse histogram for a model fit to each individual coincidence.

original_title: Total synthesis and biological evaluation of B-ring prenylated flavonoids
title: Prenylated flavonoids made from scratch
blurb: Total synthesis of B-ring prenylated flavonoids, with the resulting compounds carried through biological evaluation.

original_title: Diketone‐Functionalized [2.2]Paracyclophanes: Synthesis and Application as Photoinitiators for Two‐Photon 3D Microprinting
title: [2.2]paracyclophane gets drafted as a photoinitiator
blurb: A series of diketone-functionalized [2.2]paracyclophanes built and screened as photoinitiators for two-photon 3D microprinting, the first systematic look at whether PCP's rigid, distinctly three-dimensional scaffold is actually useful for that job.

original_title: Radical Sorting Enables Semiconductor-Driven Redox-Neutral C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) Cross-Coupling
title: Sorting radicals so they don't just homocouple
blurb: Carbon nitride photocatalysis generates alkyl radicals two ways at once, oxidizing carboxylic acids and reducing redox-active esters, and nickel sorts the pair into a cross-coupled sp3-sp3 bond instead of letting them dimerize into junk. Redox-neutral, no stoichiometric oxidant or reductant needed, which is the part that makes this more than a lab curiosity.

original_title: A scalable three-unit continuous operation platform for efficient porphyrin production
title: Porphyrins get an assembly line
blurb: Three stages running continuously, microbial fermentation into thermostable whole-cell catalysis into chemical derivatization, chain together to make porphyrin intermediates and derivatives that conventional biosynthesis can't reach. The pitch is scale, and stacking three processes end to end is the part worth watching.

original_title: Photocatalytic 1,2‐Boron Migrative Alkene Homologation to Access 1,3‐Difunctionalized Alkenes
title: Making alkenes skip a carbon via boron migration
blurb: Visible-light photocatalysis plus a traceless tert-butylsulfonyl leaving group drives a contra-thermodynamic 1,2-boron shift, moving the boron one carbon over and regenerating the alkene so you land 1,3-difunctionalized products instead of the usual vicinal ones. Remote alkene difunctionalization has been the hard one, and this does it under mild conditions with broad functional group tolerance.

original_title: Imaging of Endoplasmic Reticulum Peroxynitrite Reveals a Peroxynitrite−Protein Disulfide Isomerase Axis Driving Proteostasis Disruption in Cerebral Ischemia−Reperfusion Injury
title: Watching peroxynitrite wreck the ER during stroke reperfusion
blurb: A near-infrared probe, BDB-FD, parks itself in the ER lumen and crosses the blood-brain barrier, letting it track peroxynitrite buildup during cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in real time. First spatiotemporal map of that damage, and it fingers a peroxynitrite-PDI axis as the driver behind the proteostasis collapse.

original_title: Programmable Imaging of Locus-Specific DNA Repair Dynamics Reveals Chromatin-Controlled Therapy Resistance in Cancer
title: Tagging one gene locus to watch it get repaired live
blurb: GLIDRE uses CRISPR-guided elastin-like protein droplets to light up a single non-repetitive genomic locus, so double-strand break repair there can be watched directly instead of inferred from bulk assays. The payoff is linking chromatin state at that locus to therapy resistance in cancer cells.

original_title: Prostate Cancer Foundation of Australia Highlights Barriers to Radiopharmaceutical Access - Oncodaily
title: Australia's prostate cancer group says radiopharmaceuticals aren't reaching patients
blurb: The Prostate Cancer Foundation of Australia is calling out barriers to radiopharmaceutical access in the country. It's an advocacy flag rather than a data release, but it's coming from the group that actually treats these patients.

original_title: De novo design of antiviral monobody binders
title: Designing monobodies on a computer instead of screening for them
blurb: MobGen is a computational pipeline for designing antigen-specific monobodies from scratch, the E. coli-expressible antibody mimics, skipping the usual giant randomized library screens. A real shortcut if the hit rate holds, but de novo binder design has a habit of looking better on paper than in the assay.

original_title: A GRPR-targeted near-infrared fluorescent probe for precise tumor imaging and intraoperative surgical navigation
title: A bombesin-tagged dye for finding tumor margins mid-surgery
blurb: IR783-BBN pairs a near-infrared dye with a bombesin peptide to light up GRPR-expressing tumors, and the fluorescence matched up with histology on the excised tissue. Standard fluorescence-guided surgery pitch, still needs to clear the jump from animal model to actual OR.

original_title: Digital bioassay using a femtoliter reactor array device.
title: Running bioassays in femtoliter-sized wells
blurb: A protocol for digital bioassays using an array of femtoliter reactors, shrinking reaction volumes down to single-molecule counting territory. Methods-paper territory rather than a new finding, but that's the genre.

original_title: Multicomponent 3,6-Bisselenylation of Carbazoles with Se Powder and Boronic Acids
title: Putting selenium on carbazoles without a metal catalyst
blurb: IBr catalyzes a multicomponent radical bisselenylation that installs selenium at the 3 and 6 positions of carbazoles straight from elemental Se powder and boronic acids, moderate to excellent yields. No transition metal, no stoichiometric oxidant, no nasty selenyl precursor needed, cheap feedstock chemistry doing a job usually reserved for metal catalysis.

original_title: Need suggestions to improve the yield of an ester aminolysis reaction
title: Need suggestions to improve the yield of an ester aminolysis reaction

original_title: Plugin that draws mechanisms and structures from a text description
title: Plugin that draws mechanisms and structures from a text description
blurb: I built a plugin for Claude that draws curly-arrow mechanisms, structures and catalytic cycles from a plain description, and checks valences, stereochemistry and electron flow before showing the figure. It handles natural products and bridged ring systems too. Free and open source, and I’d welcome reports of anything it draws wrongly: https://github.com/montybwolfe/bondline [link]   [comments]

original_title: Trifunctional Pyrrolidine-Carbamate Self-Immolative Spacers Decouple Enzymatic Activation from Drug Release in Antibody-Drug Conjugates.
title: Splitting the ADC linker's two jobs apart
blurb: A pyrrolidine-carbamate spacer built so the enzyme that cuts the linker and the step that actually releases the drug aren't the same event, letting each be tuned on its own instead of being yoked together. The pitch is control over release kinetics independent of cleavage, which is normally the hard part of ADC linker design.

original_title: Digestion and Orthogonal Click Conjugation Enables Nanopore Reading of Proteins.
title: Protein sequencing is trying to copy DNA's nanopore trick
blurb: Digest the protein into peptides, then tag the fragments with orthogonal click chemistry so a nanopore can actually read them in order. Nanopore protein reading has been promised for a while without a general method showing up, so I'd want to see this work on more than a handful of test proteins first.

original_title: Synthesis and Characterization of Aminooxy Click Chemistry-Mediated Bis-Conjugates of siRNAs and Evaluation of Their RNAi Activity.
title: Hanging two payloads off one siRNA strand
blurb: Aminooxy click chemistry builds bis-conjugates, two groups stitched onto a single siRNA, and they checked the RNAi silencing still works after the extra decoration.

original_title: Lysosome-Targeting Chimeras as Clearing Agents for Pretargeted ImmunoSPECT.
title: Repurposing LYTACs to clean up after pretargeted imaging
blurb: Pretargeted ImmunoSPECT needs the circulating antibody cleared out before the radiolabeled probe goes in, and this turns lysosome-targeting chimeras into that clearing agent. A reuse of LYTACs for plumbing rather than their usual job of degrading the target itself.

original_title: Targeted alpha therapy for solid tumors: biological rationale, clinical advances, and future perspectives.
title: A grand tour of alpha therapy's state in solid tumors
blurb: A review laying out the biological case for targeted alpha therapy in solid tumors alongside where the clinical trials currently stand. Useful as an overview, but it's a review, not new data.

original_title: Hetero-Cross-Linking of Peptides Enabled by Solvent-Regulated Diazo-Type Esterification of Carboxylic Acids.
title: Cross-linking peptides by just changing the solvent
blurb: A diazo-type esterification of carboxylic acids that hetero-cross-links two different peptides, with solvent alone dialing the selectivity. Neat if it holds up past whatever model peptides they ran it on.

original_title: Investigation of the pharmacokinetics, metabolism, and clearance pathways of a heterobifunctional BRM degrader delivered by a TROP2-targeting antibody.
title: Tracking where a TROP2-targeted degrader conjugate actually goes
blurb: Pharmacokinetics and metabolism workup for a heterobifunctional BRM degrader riding a TROP2-targeting antibody, mapping how it gets cleared in vivo. The plumbing work that has to get done before anyone trusts the dosing.

original_title: A VAPG Incorporating Targeted Self-Assembling Peptides for Efficient VSMC Restoring and Imaging in Abdominal Aortic Models.
title: Self-assembling peptides aimed at rebuilding aortic smooth muscle
blurb: A VAPG-targeted self-assembling peptide system built to both restore vascular smooth muscle cells and image them in abdominal aortic models. Pairing the therapeutic and the imaging readout in one peptide is the actual pitch.

original_title: A rapidly internalizing, tetravalent antibody-drug conjugate leads to high selectivity in T-ALL cell lines due to surface antigen depletion.
title: A four-armed ADC that eats its own target to stay selective
blurb: Going tetravalent speeds up internalization, and in T-ALL cell lines that fast uptake strips the surface antigen quickly enough to make the conjugate highly selective. The selectivity trick is depleting the target, not just binding it tightly, but it's cell lines only so far.

original_title: A preclinical investigation of (135)La-labelled SSTR2 agonist and antagonist for Auger electron therapy.
title: La-135 Auger therapy: agonist versus antagonist, head to head
blurb: A preclinical comparison of La-135-labelled SSTR2 agonist and antagonist peptides for Auger electron therapy, which only pays off if the isotope parks right next to the DNA. Early cell and animal work, but the agonist-versus-antagonist comparison is the useful part here.

original_title: A FAM-Binding Bispecific Antibody for Productive Delivery of siRNA to Skin by Light-Activatable Silencing
title: A bispecific antibody that waits for a light switch before dumping siRNA into skin
blurb: siRNA does great in the liver and badly almost everywhere else, mostly because it gets stuck in the endosome. This Fab-scFv-Fc antibody grabs exactly one FAM-tagged siRNA molecule, forms a stable monodisperse complex, and only releases its cargo into skin tissue once you hit it with light. A real fix for the escape bottleneck, assuming skin isn't a special case.

original_title: Comparative analysis of early DNA damage in three human cell models exposed to Lu-177 and Tb-161 radionuclides using Geant4-DNA simulation toolkit
title: Simulating whose DNA damage is worse, Lu-177's or Tb-161's
blurb: A Geant4-DNA toolkit comparison of early DNA damage across three human cell models exposed to Lu-177 versus Tb-161, the two radionuclides currently competing for targeted radiotherapy duty. Pure simulation, no cells actually irradiated, so it's a prediction to be checked against real dosimetry later.

original_title: Analytical performance of plastic scintillation microspheres versus a liquid scintillation cocktail for measuring beta-emitting radionuclides in representative aqueous media
title: Plastic beads vs the classic liquid cocktail for counting beta decays in water
blurb: A head-to-head of plastic scintillation microspheres against standard liquid scintillation cocktail for measuring beta-emitting radionuclides in real aqueous samples. Unglamorous analytical chemistry, but it's the kind of comparison that decides what a water-monitoring lab actually buys.

original_title: De Novo Design of Single–Crystalline Peptide Frameworks Enables Structure–Encoded Molecular Recognition
title: Getting peptides to crystallize into actual binding pockets instead of fibers
blurb: Peptide self-assembly usually collapses into one-dimensional fibers because hydrogen bonding only wants to grow in one direction. Coordination-driven reprogramming of the beta-sheet packing gets around that, producing single-crystalline peptide frameworks with ordered, structurally encoded cavities that do real molecular recognition instead of just tangling into fibrils.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: A rapidly internalizing, tetravalent antibody-drug conjugate leads to high selectivity in T-ALL cell lines due to surface antigen depletion
title: A tetravalent ADC that wins selectivity by stripping the target off the cell
blurb: A fast-internalizing, four-valent antibody-drug conjugate that gets its selectivity in T-ALL cell lines by rapidly depleting the surface antigen itself, not just by delivering a nastier payload. Cell-line data for now.

original_title: Photochemical Isomerization of Dilithiobutadienes to Dilithium Salts of Cyclobutadiene Dianions
title: Light turns dilithiobutadienes into the dianion salts chemists couldn't easily get to
blurb: Shine visible light on tetraaryl or disilyl-diaryl 1,4-dilithiobutadienes with THF, DME, or TMEDA around and they isomerize cleanly into the corresponding dilithium cyclobutadiene dianion salts. Routes to this dianion have always been rare and awkward, so a clean photochemical path that also reaches new substitution patterns is the actual news here, niche as the target is.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Advanced Antibody–Drug Conjugate Structural Characterization by Sheathless Capillary Electrophoresis–Tandem Mass Spectrometry Using Complementary Approaches - Spectroscopy Online
title: Characterizing ADCs by CE-MS without the sheath liquid
blurb: A trade-press rundown on using sheathless capillary electrophoresis tandem mass spectrometry, alongside complementary methods, to pick apart antibody-drug conjugate structure. More a QC toolkit writeup than a finding, but useful if ADC heterogeneity is your actual job.

original_title: Stereodivergent γ-Propargylation of α,β-Unsaturated Aldehydes
title: Picking your stereochemistry on demand in γ-propargylation
blurb: First stereodivergent γ-propargylation of α,β-unsaturated aldehydes: racemic propargylic acetates plus a Cu(I)/Pybox or Cu(I)/phosphine complex paired with a diphenylprolinol silyl ether, and the catalyst combo you pick sets which of the two new adjacent stereocenters you get, with clean γ-selectivity and E-selectivity throughout. Cooperative catalysis finally showing up somewhere it had mostly skipped.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: A Tailor-Made Guanidine Ionizable Lipid as a Bifunctional mRNA Carrier and Nitric Oxide Production Inhibitor
title: An ionizable lipid that carries mRNA and tells the macrophages to calm down
blurb: LNPs are the default mRNA delivery platform, but they tend to provoke macrophage-driven inflammation that nobody's fully solved. This design embeds a nitric oxide-inhibiting motif directly into the ionizable lipid, so one molecule delivers mRNA and suppresses the inflammatory response at the same time. Screening a focused acyl-guanidine library in LPS-triggered peritoneal macrophages turned up G9 as the potent hit, still a cell-culture result.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Optimizing radon quantification in arid groundwater: Counting-time strategies and QA/QC for sub-Bq·L<sup>−1</sup> measurements
title: Squeezing a trustworthy radon number out of arid groundwater
blurb: A practical look at counting-time strategies and QA/QC needed to actually hit sub-Bq/L sensitivity when measuring radon in groundwater from arid regions. Not a new method, just the unglamorous work of figuring out how long you need to count before you believe the number.

original_title: Overcoming Ru-99 Isobaric Overlap via C2H4 as a Reaction Gas for Tc-99 Accurate Measurement in Large-Volume Seawater Samples by Triple Quadrupole ICP−MS with Mass-Shift Mode
title: Swapping math for chemistry to kill the Ru-99 interference in Tc-99 seawater analysis
blurb: Tc-99 measurements in seawater get fouled by Ru-99 and Mo-98 overlap, and the usual fix, correcting via a known Ru isotope ratio, just drags the uncertainty up. This one runs triple-quad ICP-MS with C2H4 as a mass-shift reaction gas instead, pulling accurate Tc-99 numbers out of 20+ liter seawater samples without leaning on an assumed ratio.

original_title: Tunable Na2Re3S y Se6– y ( y = 0–6) Chalcogenides via BCM-Flux Synthesis: Structure, Compositional Control, and Electronic Properties
title: Dialing sulfur and selenium into a Re cluster chalcogenide like a slider
blurb: A boron-chalcogen flux method grows Na2Re3SySe6-y crystals across the full S-to-Se range, with the lattice expanding on cue as Se goes in. Mostly a structure-and-synthesis paper, solid crystallography on both end members, electronic properties tagging along.

original_title: Photoredox Deoxygenative Activation of α,β-Unsaturated Carboxylic Acids for the Synthesis of Aza-γ-Lactams
title: Making radicals from unsaturated acids without just decarboxylating them
blurb: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acids usually just decarboxylate when you try to activate them, so the trick here is a phosphine-assisted photoredox setup that strips oxygen instead, generating cinnamoyl radicals that go on to do a [3+2] with azoarenes and build aza-γ-lactams directly, no need to pre-activate the substrate. 35 examples up to 78% yield, with DFT backing a radical-relay mechanism.

original_title: Photoinduced Decavanadate-Catalyzed Radical Polar Crossover Enables Selective C(sp3)–H Amination
title: A vanadium photocatalyst that lets C-H amination use the amines everyone else's method can't
blurb: Decavanadate HAT photocatalysis paired with radical-polar crossover sidesteps the chemoselectivity problem that's dogged C(sp3)-H amination: existing radical-polar protocols choke on easily-oxidized primary heteroaryl amines, and this one couples them directly anyway, using xanthene and dihydroacridine-type donors as the H source.

original_title: Metabolic and nutritional toxicities associated with antibody-drug conjugates: a combined analysis of a pediatric relapsed/refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia cohort and the FAERS database
title: Tallying the metabolic damage from an ADC in kids with relapsed leukemia
blurb: Pairs a real pediatric cohort, 146 kids with relapsed/refractory B-ALL on inotuzumab ozogamicin or other salvage therapy, with a trawl through FAERS for ADC-linked metabolic and nutrition adverse event signals. The nutrition side of ADC toxicity barely gets looked at, so this is filling in a gap rather than overturning anything.

original_title: Organocatalytic Asymmetric Multicomponent Dearomatizing Povarov Reactions
title: Three components, one pot, five stereocenters out of a Povarov reaction
blurb: An organocatalytic asymmetric Povarov that dearomatizes as it goes, stacking up a quaternary stereocenter and four new rings in a single step, up to 99% yield, >50:1 dr, 98% ee. The kind of step-count flex that's genuinely hard to fake with a catalyst alone.

original_title: Intramolecular, Formal [3 + 2]-Annulation of Indoles with Allenylidene-Butenolides of Nucleophile Intercepted Meyer–Schuster Rearrangement: Access to Polycyclic Spiroindolines (Indeno[1,7 a-b ]indoles)
title: Trapping a Meyer-Schuster intermediate with an indole instead of letting it react normally
blurb: The oxonium intermediates from nucleophile-intercepted Meyer-Schuster rearrangements are normally just 1,2-bis-electrophiles, but here they're wired up intramolecularly to an appended indole for a formal [3+2], routing through a spiroindoleninium to build indeno-indole spiroindolines. Niche intermediate, genuinely new ring system out of it.

original_title: Synthesis of Axially, Planar and Helically Chiral Molecules via Rhodium-Catalyzed Asymmetric C–H Functionalization Reactions
title: Rhodium's run at building chirality that isn't a stereocenter
blurb: A conspectus on using Rh-catalyzed asymmetric C-H functionalization to build axial, planar, and helical chirality instead of the usual point stereocenters, the scaffolds that keep showing up as privileged ligands and catalysts. Review, not new data, but a useful map of how far C-H activation has pushed into that space.

original_title: Vinylcyclopropanes in Rearrangement Reactions
title: Sixty years of vinylcyclopropanes picking themselves apart
blurb: A review of vinylcyclopropane rearrangement and cycloisomerization chemistry, the strain-release reactions, both homolytic and heterolytic, that have made this one small strained motif into a long-running source of ring complexity. Survey piece, useful if you need the state of the field in one place.

original_title: Probing Electron-Spin Redistribution in Trimetallic FeMoFe Complexes
title: Watching spin shuffle between iron and molybdenum in one three-metal complex
blurb: A trimetallic FeMoFe platform caught across two redox states, one half-integer spin, one diamagnetic, with spectroscopy showing the electrons aren't cleanly localized on any one metal: the 1+ state comes out as an intermediate-spin Fe, a low-spin Fe, and a low-spin Mo all coupling together. Basic bioinorganic electronic-structure work, aimed at the Fe-Mo cooperation question in small-molecule activation chemistry.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Planar-Chiral Cyclophanes: From Synthetic Strategies to Configurational Stability Control.
title: A review of how to keep planar-chiral cyclophanes from flipping back
blurb: An Acc Chem Res rundown of synthetic routes to planar-chiral cyclophanes and what actually keeps the chirality locked in once you've made it. No new chemistry here, just the state of the art collected in one place.

original_title: Antibody full-length light chain reshapes variable domains aggregation without altering their dominance in amyloid fibrils
title: The light chain's full-length form slows amyloid aggregation but doesn't call the shots
blurb: Using a patient's own light chain, the full-length form transiently grabs the truncated VL fragment, cutting its aggregation rate almost fourfold and pushing it toward fibrils that are protease-sensitive and bad at seeding new aggregation. But VL still ends up dominating the final fibrils regardless, so FL changes the path, not the destination.

original_title: TDCR++ a code for radionuclide metrology in liquid scintillation and decay-data sensitivity analysis
title: A new code for squeezing more certainty out of liquid scintillation counting
blurb: TDCR++ handles radionuclide metrology in liquid scintillation counting and runs sensitivity analysis on the decay data feeding it. Infrastructure paper, the kind nobody cites but everyone's activity numbers quietly depend on.

original_title: N-Heterocyclic Carbene (NHC)-Catalyzed Synthesis of Atropisomers Beyond C–C Axial Chirality
title: NHC catalysis takes atropisomers past the usual biaryl C–C axis
blurb: A conspectus on using N-heterocyclic carbene catalysis to build atropisomers around C–N, C–O, and N–N axes, not just the well-trodden biaryl C–C kind. Those axes have lower rotational barriers and are more prone to just spinning back to racemic, which is exactly why getting a handle on them with NHC catalysis is the notable part.

original_title: Selenium-Containing Polymers: In Vivo Modulation and Radioprotection.
title: Selenium polymers doing radioprotection duty in vivo
blurb: An Acc Chem Res review on selenium-containing polymers and their role modulating radioprotection in living systems. Thin on specifics here, but selenium's redox chemistry pulling double duty as a radioprotectant is the throughline.

original_title: Radiopharmaceutical Therapy as a Particle Therapy: A Case for Convergence with Radiation Oncology.
title: Making the case that radiopharma is just another kind of particle therapy
blurb: An argument piece for treating radiopharmaceutical therapy as a particle therapy in its own right, and pushing radiation oncology and radiopharma to actually talk to each other instead of running as parallel fields. A positioning paper more than a data one.
venue: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys

original_title: CO2 reductive amination-enabled stereodivergent hydrocyanation of alkynes
title: Hydrocyanation without the cyanide, courtesy of CO2 and ammonia
blurb: Nickel catalysis builds nitriles from alkynes using amidate intermediates made from CO2/NH3 instead of free cyanide, sidestepping both the toxicity and the usual problem of cyanide binding nickel too tightly to be useful. Swap in KF as the additive and you get up to 95% Z-selectivity, with the stereodivergence itself being the actual selling point.

original_title: Highly active supported nickel phosphide catalyst for the semi-hydrogenation of complex, densely functionalized alkynes
title: A nickel phosphide catalyst gunning for Lindlar's job
blurb: Lindlar's Pd/Pb catalyst has stayed the default for alkyne semi-hydrogenation because nothing else matches its substrate scope. This nickel phosphide catalyst is pitched as a lead-free, noble-metal-free alternative that handles complex, densely functionalized alkynes rather than just the easy textbook substrates, which is usually where Lindlar replacements fall apart.

original_title: Axial Chirality Tuned by CH∙∙∙FC Nonconventional Hydrogen Bonds
title: Weak CH…F hydrogen bonds doing real work on axial chirality
blurb: Variable-temperature NMR and X-ray structures on fluorinated anilides show restricted rotation around the aryl–C–N bond, held up by CH…F-C nonconventional hydrogen bonds alongside stereoelectronic effects. DFT and NBO analysis back it up: these weak interactions are stabilizing the ground state enough to actually set the rotational barrier, not just decorate the crystal structure.

original_title: Rational Design of Molecular Glue Degraders Utilizing Endogenous Transient Protein-Protein Interactions
title: Designing molecular glues by exploiting protein handshakes that already happen
blurb: TrIP-MGRD is a rational design strategy for molecular glue degraders that targets druggable pockets at transient protein-protein interfaces that already form on their own, instead of screening blind for compounds that create new ones. They demonstrate it on CDK12, which makes this proof of concept more than a drug yet.

original_title: Elucidation of a ThiF-Like Enzyme-Mediated Biosynthetic Pathway for Scalemic N -Acyl Amides with Antiangiogenic Activity
title: A bacterial enzyme that builds its own chiral mix on purpose
blurb: PdfB, a standalone ThiF-family adenylyltransferase from the marine bacterium Pseudovibrio denitrificans, makes N-acyl amides that come out racemic, scalemic, or fully enantiopure depending on the metabolite, all by generating one electrophilic oxazolone intermediate and trapping it stepwise. The amides have antiangiogenic activity, but the real find is a bacterial pathway that actually controls its own chirality instead of defaulting to one or the other.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Programmable Charge Separation in Heteroleptic Donor–Acceptor Metallacages for Efficient Visible‐Light‐Driven Cross‐Dehydrogenative Coupling
title: Tuning a metal cage's electronics to make it photocatalyze better
blurb: Heteroleptic Pt(II) metallacages built from perylene diimide acceptors and swappable donor ligands, where making the donor more electron-rich programs how fast charge separates inside the cage. More separation translates to better visible-light cross-dehydrogenative coupling. A clean structure-to-activity knob, though it's demonstrated on one reaction class so far.

original_title: Prediction and Determination of Monolayer Structure in Binary Ligand Mixtures on Gold Nanoparticles
title: What two ligands actually do to each other on a gold nanoparticle
blurb: A systematic study of carboxyl- and amine-terminated alkanethiols mixed with methyl-terminated ones on gold nanoparticles, working out which physical and chemical forces actually dictate how the two ligands sort themselves across the surface. Groundwork for anyone designing nanoparticle interfaces who's been guessing at monolayer morphology rather than predicting it.

original_title: Mechanisms of Ammonia Synthesis over Ru Low- and High-Index Surfaces Based on Density Functional Theory Calculations
title: DFT digs into why ruthenium beats iron at making ammonia
blurb: Density functional theory compares low- and high-index ruthenium surfaces for ammonia synthesis, chasing why Ru's higher intrinsic activity might let the reaction run milder than Haber-Bosch's iron process at 400-500°C and 200 atm. Mechanistic insight only, calculations rather than a working reactor, but it's the kind of energetics mapping that catalyst design actually needs.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Measurement of activity size distribution of radon and thoron progeny using DRPS/DTPS based cascade impactor
title: Sizing up radon's decay products with a cascade impactor
blurb: A DRPS/DTPS-based cascade impactor measurement of the activity size distribution for radon and thoron progeny, the unglamorous aerosol dosimetry that radiation exposure estimates quietly rest on.

original_title: Synthesis of Katritzky Salts from Cyclopropyl, Allyl, Propargyl, and Benzyl Alcohols
title: Katritzky salts without the amine, starting from alcohols instead
blurb: Katritzky salts are normally built from amines, but this route gets there from cyclopropyl, allyl, propargyl, or benzyl alcohols, via triflate intermediates that alkylate 2,4,6-triphenylpyridine. The cyclopropyl triflates even rearrange to allylic ones along the way, a nice bit of mechanism tucked inside what's otherwise a new precursor scope for radical-coupling chemistry.

original_title: Evolution-Guided Engineering of a Process-Compatible Thymidine Phosphorylase for the Scalable Cascade Biosynthesis of 2′/3′-Functionalized Purine Nucleoside Analogs
title: Ancestor-reconstructed enzyme makes nucleoside analogs that survive scale-up
blurb: Ancestral sequence reconstruction plus kcat/Km virtual screening turns up ASR114, a thymidine phosphorylase variant tuned to stay active under actual process conditions rather than just in a test tube. That's the part that usually kills nucleoside-analog biocatalysis at scale, so a variant that doesn't fall apart is the whole point here.

original_title: Plasma-Polymerized Coatings Retaining Oxidized-Sulfur Functionalities for Liquid-Interface Applications
title: Getting plasma coatings to keep their sulfur groups once they're wet
blurb: Plasma-polymerized coatings usually shed their functional groups after extended time in liquid. This one pairs a hybrid TFMSA/sodium styrenesulfonate precursor chemistry with rapid thermal annealing to keep oxidized sulfur intact inside a carboxyl-rich matrix, laid down in one step by atmospheric-pressure plasma. Durability at the solid-liquid interface is the actual claim, not just that the coating can be made.

original_title: FRET-Based Single-Molecule Detection of Pathogens.
title: Single-molecule FRET as a pathogen detector
blurb: Single-molecule FRET used to flag pathogens directly, detection at the individual-particle level rather than the usual bulk-assay average.

original_title: Nickel-Catalyzed Reductive Three-Component Cross-Coupling of Butadiene with Chiral N - tert -Butanesulfinyl Imines and Alkenyl Triflates or Aryl Iodides: Access to Enantioenriched Homoallylic Amines
title: Three components, one nickel catalyst, enantioenriched homoallylic amines
blurb: A nickel-catalyzed reductive coupling stitches together butadiene, chiral N-tert-butanesulfinyl imines, and alkenyl triflates or aryl iodides in one pot, landing 1,4-disubstituted homoallylic amines with both regio- and stereocontrol. They ran it gram-scale and pushed the products through further transformations, so it's not just a scope table of small-batch examples.

original_title: Electrochemical-Flow Scholl Reaction of Tris(diarylamino)benzenes en Route to Azatruxenes
title: Electrochemical flow builds azatruxenes, which then make their own photocatalyst
blurb: An e-flow Scholl reaction where dialing the voltage controls a cascade cyclization of triarylamines into azatruxenes, cleanly and selectively. Then they just grind the product with electron acceptors to get charge-transfer complexes that catalyze H2O2 production. The synthesis is the real work here, the photocatalysis reads like a bonus demo.

original_title: ATTEC-Based Autophagic Elimination of HBV Core Protein Achieves Potent Viral Suppression
title: A degrader for HBV core protein instead of just jamming it
blurb: Core protein allosteric modulators bind HBc but can't clear it and resistance keeps showing up. TK-96 fuses one of those modulators (NVR3-778) to an LC3 ligand to make an ATTEC that drags both wild-type and drug-resistant HBc into the autophagy-lysosome pathway for degradation. Degrading the target instead of just blocking it is the point, and it's the kind of trick that could dodge the resistance problem CpAMs keep running into.

original_title: MolMap resolves functional chromatin responses to small-molecule perturbation
title: Mapping where a small molecule actually does something to chromatin, not just where it sticks
blurb: MolMap profiles isolated, non-crosslinked nuclei genome-wide to find where a compound triggers a functional chromatin response, skipping the usual proxies of binding sites, protein occupancy, or downstream expression. Going straight for function instead of inferring it from where something parks is the useful part.

original_title: Alginate-DNA Core-Shell Hydrogel Microspheres Program Antigen Release Kinetics for Potent Single-Dose Subunit Vaccination.
title: Core-shell hydrogel beads that meter out antigen for a one-shot vaccine
blurb: Alginate-DNA microspheres with a core-shell structure built to program the release kinetics of antigen, aiming for a single-dose subunit vaccine instead of a prime-boost schedule. The snippet's thin on numbers, but the idea is using the shell as a timer.

original_title: Dosimetric and biological characterization of a three-dimensional cell co-culture model for the evaluation of specific and nonspecific effects induced by targeted radiopharmaceuticals.
title: A 3D co-culture model for sorting out what radiopharmaceuticals actually do to which cells
blurb: Dosimetric and biological characterization of a 3D co-culture setup meant to separate specific from nonspecific effects of targeted radiopharmaceuticals. Not much detail to go on beyond that, but it's the kind of model that matters for trusting dose-response numbers from simpler single-cell assays.

original_title: Transannular Sigmatropic Rearrangement of Transient Spirocyclic C3 Ammonium Ylides: Stereospecific Access to Bridged Bicyclic Benzo[ b ]azepine Derivatives and Higher Homologues
title: A [1,5] carbon shift turns aziridine chalcones into bridged benzazepines
blurb: Enantiopure aziridine-substituted chalcones go through a transient spirocyclic ammonium ylide that rearranges via an unusual [1,5] carbon shift, giving benzo[b]azepin-6-ones in good yields with full retention of stereochemistry. They stretch the same trick to bigger rings, azocines and azecines, and back it up with DFT and NBO analysis. Full stereo transfer on a ring expansion like this is the part worth noticing.

original_title: Solvent‐Controlled Site‐Switchable C–H Alkylation of Quinolines
title: Pick your solvent, pick which C-H bond on the quinoline reacts
blurb: Quinoline N-oxides plus dialkyl acetylenedicarboxylates give different regiochemistry just by swapping solvent: trifluoroethanol pushes a dearomative [3,3] rearrangement to C8-alkylation, while another solvent routes it elsewhere. Getting site-divergent selectivity from condition tweaks alone, no new catalyst or directing group, is the trick that makes this useful rather than just another C-H paper.

original_title: Characterizing Biopharmaceutical Materials with Neutron Scattering
title: A review on using neutron scattering to look at protein drugs
blurb: A review of neutron scattering's growing use on biopharmaceutical materials: protein and excipient structure in solution, protein-protein interactions, that sort of thing. Useful for the sensitivity to light elements and isotope labeling, less useful if you wanted new results rather than a survey of what's been done.

original_title: Avenzo Therapeutics Presents Positive Preliminary Results from the Phase 1 Study of AVZO-1418, a Potentially Best-in-Class EGFR/HER3 Bispecific Antibody-Drug Conjugate, at the 38th EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium - Business Wire
title: Avenzo's bispecific ADC posts early phase 1 numbers it's calling best-in-class
blurb: A press release on AVZO-1418, an EGFR/HER3 bispecific antibody-drug conjugate, with preliminary phase 1 data shown at EORTC-NCI-AACR. "Potentially best-in-class" is the company's own framing on its own early results, so treat it as a conference teaser rather than a verdict.

original_title: Investigations into Gas-Phase Formation in Glass CRMs during LA-ICP-MS
title: Glass reference materials quietly vaporize some elements during laser ablation
blurb: Gas-phase formation during LA-ICP-MS was thought to be an organic-matrix quirk, seen in things like gelatine. Pulse-resolved LA-ICP-TOFMS on NIST glass standards SRM 610 and 612 finds measurable gaseous transport too, for Zn, Ge, As, Cd, Sn, and Sb specifically, while the rest of the elements tested stayed particulate. Worth knowing if you've been trusting glass CRMs as the clean, all-particulate calibration case.

original_title: Recent advances in fabrication strategies, functional modulation and healthcare applications of native protein-based hydrogels.
title: A grand tour of protein hydrogels, no single result
blurb: A review stitching together how native protein hydrogels get made, tuned, and pointed at healthcare uses. No new data here, just the state of the field in one place.

original_title: Revealing Bulk-Phase Reactivity of Fe-Based Catalyst in the Reverse Water–Gas Shift Reaction
title: Iron catalysts don't stay put at the surface
blurb: Microscopy, isotope labeling, and ML-driven molecular dynamics on an Fe catalyst running the reverse water-gas shift show the chemistry isn't confined to the surface. Under reaction conditions the catalyst restructures into a dynamic FeOx/Fe3C mixed phase that pushes reactivity into the bulk, which is a problem for the usual surface-only picture of heterogeneous catalysis.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: H-Bonding-Assisted Strategy for the Construction of Isoreticular Lanthanide-Based MOFs from 1,4-Benzenedihydroxamic Acid
title: Pinning down a floppy linker so lanthanide MOFs actually crystallize in a series
blurb: Hydroxamate MOFs are stable but the flexible -NH- linker usually wrecks any attempt at a clean isoreticular series. Adding formate as an H-bond acceptor stiffens it enough to build four matched lanthanide MOFs (Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy) off the same benzenedihydroxamic acid ligand. A structural fix more than a new material, but a useful one.

original_title: Nanotechnology-Driven (18)F-FDG Imaging to Understand the Change in Insulin Sensitivity: Current Evidence, Methodological Gaps, and Translational Challenges.
title: Nanotech wants in on 18F-FDG imaging of insulin sensitivity, evidence still catching up
blurb: A review of using nanotech-enhanced 18F-FDG PET to track changes in insulin sensitivity, laying out what's been shown so far plus the methodological and translational gaps still open. A roadmap, not a result.

original_title: Site‐Inverted Balz–Schiemann Type Para ‐Fluorination
title: A Balz-Schiemann fluorination that hits the wrong carbon on purpose
blurb: A century of Balz-Schiemann chemistry has always put the new fluorine where the diazo group was. This flips it: palladium catalysis plus a migrating directing group delivers the fluorine para to the original diazonium site instead, under mild conditions. Para-selective aryl fluorination is exactly the position that's normally hardest to hit directly.

original_title: Development of a Concise Synthesis of Glycinoeclepin A, a Picomolar Soybean Cyst Nematode Hatching Factor
title: A shorter route to the hormone that makes nematode eggs hatch themselves to death
blurb: Glycinoeclepin A triggers soybean cyst nematode eggs into suicidal hatching at picomolar concentrations, which makes it an appealing pesticide except nobody can get enough of it made. This account covers two synthetic strategies toward a more concise total synthesis, one building the vicinal quaternary centers off a cyclopropane via Claisen-type condensation. Still a account of routes, not a report of kilograms in hand.

original_title: Medicines Discovery Catapult and Astral Systems secure £1.54m to develop “radiopharmaceutical lab of the future” - Insider Media Ltd
title: £1.54m to build a 'radiopharmaceutical lab of the future'
blurb: Medicines Discovery Catapult and Astral Systems pick up £1.54m to develop faster radiopharma lab infrastructure. Money for the plumbing, not a drug.

original_title: Kyntra axes mid-stage ADC, adding to years of stumbles
title: Kyntra cuts its mid-stage ADC, keeps the losing streak going
blurb: Formerly FibroGen, now renamed Kyntra Bio, the company axes a clinical antibody-drug conjugate from its pipeline, the latest in a run of setbacks for an outfit that can't seem to catch a break.

original_title: Irradiation‐Wavelength‐Tuned Stepwise [2+2] Cycloaddition of Indolylphenylpropenone Derivatives as a Platform for Light–Mechanical Energy Conversion
title: Crystals that run a different [2+2] depending on the color of light you shine on them
blurb: Indolylphenylpropenone crystals undergo a stepwise [2+2] cycloaddition where blue light steers the reaction to one cyclobutane isomer over another, which only works because the molecules are already prearranged in the crystal lattice. Pitched as a platform for turning light into mechanical motion, which is the more interesting claim than the cyclobutane itself.

original_title: A dual-crosslinked herbal hydrogel for multimodal therapy of ulcerative colitis via IL-34/IL-22 modulation.
title: A double-crosslinked herbal gel that dials down two interleukins at once for ulcerative colitis
blurb: A dual-crosslinked herbal hydrogel treats ulcerative colitis by modulating both IL-34 and IL-22 rather than hitting a single target. Multimodal in the sense that it's hedging across two pathways at once.

original_title: Nanoscale Interfacial Engineering of Printable Polysaccharide Hydrogels for Simultaneous High Porosity and Wet-State Mechanical Robustness.
title: A hydrogel that's porous but doesn't fall apart wet
blurb: Printable polysaccharide hydrogels usually trade off porosity against wet-state strength; this one engineers the interfaces at the nanoscale to get both at once. Materials-journal paper, so the real test is whether it holds up outside a benchtop print.

original_title: Click and bioorthogonal chemistry in drug delivery and bioconjugation: Design principles, biological performance, and translational outlook.
title: The click chemistry literature, collected into one review
blurb: A review tracing bioorthogonal and click reactions from reagent design through biological performance to where they actually land in the clinic. A map of the field, not a new result.

original_title: Facile Maleimide-Hydrazine Reaction to Form Stable Bonds in Dynamic Hydrazone-Cross-Linked Hydrogels.
title: Locking one stable bond into an otherwise reversible hydrogel
blurb: Hydrazone cross-links give these hydrogels their dynamic, self-healing character, but a maleimide-hydrazine reaction drops in a permanent bond wherever you need one. Lets you pin down a spot without the rest of the network losing its reversibility.

original_title: His-tag-directed, stable conjugation of proteins via [CoIII(NTA/IDA)(CO3)]2−/− reagents
title: Tagging His-tagged proteins by the tag, not the protein
blurb: Cobalt(III) carbonate reagents built on NTA or IDA chelators latch onto the His-tag itself, giving a stable, site-selective conjugate under physiological conditions instead of the usual tradeoff between stability and keeping the protein functional. Works on an antibody too, which is the part worth noting.

original_title: Chemically Programmable Antibody-Drug Conjugates: Strategies from Targeting Programmability to Payload Activation
title: ADCs you could keep editing after they're already built
blurb: A review on making ADC chemistry programmable post-assembly, swapping or activating targeting and payload modules on a fixed antibody scaffold instead of locking everything in at manufacture. Strategy roundup, not a working drug.
venue: International Journal of Biology and Life Sciences

original_title: Membrane-confined self-assembly enables localized bioorthogonal prodrug activation and selective cancer therapy.
title: Confining prodrug activation to the membrane, on purpose
blurb: Self-assembly kept at the membrane localizes bioorthogonal prodrug activation right where it's wanted, giving selective killing in cancer cells. Thin on detail beyond that, but the localization trick is the whole point.
